content: The references provided are a comprehensive collection of scientific and technical documents related to water quality, sanitation, hygiene, and radiological safety. 1. Lloyd B, Bartram J (1991): This chapter discusses surveillance strategies to address microbiological issues in water quality control, particularly in developing countries. It emphasizes the importance of monitoring and implementing solutions to ensure safe drinking water. Published in Water Science and Technology, Volume 24, pages 61–75. 2. WHO (1976): This publication outlines the surveillance of drinking water quality, providing a framework for monitoring and ensuring safe water supplies. Published by the World Health Organization in Geneva. 3. WHO (1997): The second edition of the Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality provides detailed recommendations for maintaining and improving water safety. This document is a critical resource for public health professionals. 4. WHO and UNICEF (2017): This report highlights progress on drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene, serving as a baseline for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It provides data and analysis on global water and sanitation access. 5. APHA, AWWA, WEF (2005): The 21st edition of Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater offers comprehensive methodologies for analyzing water and wastewater quality. Published by the American Public Health Association, American Water Works Association, and Water Environment Federation. 6. Bartram J, Ballance R (1996): This guide focuses on the design and implementation of freshwater quality studies and monitoring programs. It is a practical resource for water quality professionals. 7. Cotruvo JA et al. (2010): This book examines the health and environmental impacts of desalination technology, providing insights into its benefits and risks. Published by CRC Press. 8. FAO/WHO (2009): This report evaluates the benefits and risks of using chlorine-containing disinfectants in food production and processing, emphasizing microbiological safety. 9. FAO/WHO (2019): This meeting report addresses the safety and quality of water used in food production and processing, with a focus on microbiological risk assessment. 10. Hutin Y, Luby S, Paquet C (2003): This study investigates a large cholera outbreak in Kano City, Nigeria, highlighting the critical role of handwashing with soap and the risks associated with street-vended water. Published in the Journal of Water and Health, Volume 1, pages 45–52. 11. Sphere Association (2018): The Sphere Handbook provides humanitarian standards for water, sanitation, and hygiene in emergency responses, ensuring minimum standards are met. 12. WHO (2005): This document, Nutrients in Drinking Water, explores the health implications of essential nutrients present in drinking water. 13. WHO (2016): The third edition of the International Health Regulations (2005) outlines global health security measures, including water safety in the context of infectious disease outbreaks. 14. WHO (2020): This publication addresses water, sanitation, hygiene, and waste management in the context of SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19. 15. WHO/WEDC (2013): Technical notes on water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) in emergencies provide practical guidance for managing water and sanitation in crisis situations. 16. AWWA (1999): The Waterborne Pathogens Manual (M48) by the American Water Works Association offers detailed information on identifying and managing waterborne pathogens. 17. Bitton G (2005): The third edition of Wastewater Microbiology provides an in-depth analysis of microbial processes in wastewater treatment. 18. Chevrefils G et al. (2006): This study quantifies the UV dose required for incremental inactivation of bacteria, protozoa, and viruses, published in IUVA News, Volume 8, pages 38–45. 19. Clasen T et al. (2006): This Cochrane Review evaluates interventions to improve water quality for preventing diarrheal diseases, emphasizing evidence-based practices. 20. Dullemont YJ et al. (2006): This chapter discusses the removal of microorganisms through slow sand filtration, published in Recent Progress in Slow Sand and Alternative Biofiltration Processes. 21. Feachem RG et al. (1983): This book, Sanitation and Disease, explores the health aspects of excreta and wastewater management, providing foundational knowledge for public health professionals. 22. Fewtrell L, Colford J (2004): This systematic review and meta-analysis examine the impact of water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions on diarrheal diseases. 23. Gerba CP et al. (1996): This risk assessment study focuses on waterborne rotavirus, published in Water Research, Volume 30, pages 2929–2940. 24. Haas CN, Rose JB, Gerba CP (1999): The book Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment provides a framework for assessing microbial risks in water systems. 25. Hijnen WAM et al. (2006): This review evaluates the inactivation of viruses, bacteria, and protozoa in water using UV radiation, published in Water Research, Volume 40, pages 3–22. 26. ISO Standards (2003–2019): A series of ISO standards provide guidance on water sampling, preservation, and analysis, ensuring consistency and reliability in water quality assessments. 27. ICRP Publications (1996–2020): The International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) provides recommendations on radiological safety, including dose assessments and protection measures for prolonged radiation exposure. 28. IAEA (2011–2018): The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) publishes safety standards and guidelines for radiological emergencies, emphasizing preparedness and response. 29. Health Canada (2009): This technical document outlines radiological parameters for Canadian drinking water quality, ensuring public health protection. 30. NAS (1999): This report assesses the risks of radon in drinking water, providing a scientific basis for regulatory decisions. 31. Picano E (2008): This article discusses the importance of informed consent and risk communication in radiological and nuclear medicine examinations, published in the British Medical Journal. 32. Rühm W et al. (2022): This study reviews current epidemiological evidence on cancer risks associated with low doses of ionizing radiation, published in Mutation Research. These references collectively provide a robust foundation for understanding water quality, sanitation, hygiene, and radiological safety, offering critical insights for public health and environmental professionals.
